_comment: Vehicle registry — the Operator Station's canonical vehicle identity, data-driven.
Loaded by vehicle_registry.load_registry() at startup (override the path with the
OPERATOR_VEHICLE_REGISTRY environment variable). Adding a USV means adding an entry
here and restarting the backend — no code change anywhere in the station.
key          canonical id, written as the slug 'usv-<n>' (the numeric id is derived
from it, or declared explicitly with 'id')
display_name what operators see. NEVER an identity: a vehicle may change it, and no
state, cache, command or selection is ever keyed by it
aliases      every other spelling THIS vehicle may use for itself in a status packet
(callsigns, hull names, bare numbers). Explicit only — the station never
guesses an alias, because a guess could merge two different vehicles.
The key, its slug and its bare number are always aliases of themselves.
An alias claimed by two vehicles is a hard startup error, not a silent last-one-wins.
SCOPE — this file is MONITORING & IDENTITY ONLY. It says who exists and how to
resolve their packets; it carries NO addresses and grants NO command reach. Live
telemetry works from a registry entry alone, because vehicles PUSH it to us via
POST /agent/status — that push path is entirely separate from the outbound map below.
Outbound vehicle-local API routing (control authority, Pixhawk mission reads,
experiment control) is a SEPARATE map, VEHICLE_API_BASE in main.py, and needs a real
verified address per vehicle. Listed here but absent there = monitored but not
commandable, which is a supported state: those endpoints answer available:false.
Never add a guessed address to close that gap.
ADDING A FUTURE USV therefore takes BOTH halves: an identity entry here AND a verified
row in VEHICLE_API_BASE. Appearing in this file alone does NOT make a vehicle
commandable. Verified routes today: usv-2 Scout http://10.0.2.10:8080, usv-3 SAR-001
http://10.0.3.10:8080 — both the vehicle Flask API on port 8080. NEVER port 8090: that
is the Local Agent diagnostics server, and it answers /agent/pixhawk_mission while
404ing /agent/control_authority and /agent/experiment/network, so a route pointed there
looks healthy on the mission pages while control silently fails.
